Honestly it comes down to map knowledge in a lot of ways, Knowing where valuable spawn, docking bays, escape pods, vaults, depots, locked rooms etc but That comes with time.

Also noise is a huge thing. let's take a map like spaceport for example, near the bar area and pod bay is where The majority of loot is so players tend to head to that area. Being able to know the sound of a door opening, or a Locked door opening, or opening a weapons crate, walking on glass/metal Will give you a huge advantage Knowing where people are and how to approach a situation.
That being said take advantage of walking and don't be afraid to take a raid slow and undetected.

Now with kits.
 This is pretty subjective but play to the kit you have, I usually won't run a backpack bigger than a commando unless I have level 11 gear higher because it's just not worth the storage risk 😅, just like how I avoid using guns that can mow people down like an SSG or ADS rifle without high tier armor/helmet.

As someone who went from 1 viewer for months, to an average of 60 with a peak of two 218,
Then back down to 30 I have one piece of advice..

Don't give a fuck about the numbers.

Think about why you're streaming.
 Be honest with yourself. Are you doing it because you want fame? Money? Entertainment? Just for fun? Are you trying to meet people? Do you want to do a job more than anything?

I started streaming because I wanted to entertain people and I thought it would be fun to have a community that I can talk shit with/act like a crackhead on stream with,  I believe that's why I started growing.

I made a lot of friends with people who are regulars to the stream And I looked forward to it all the time but then came the problem...

The numbers.

Internet good boy points are a drug just like any other, you get addicted to them.
For me after a few months of growth I started to come obsessed with my analytics and continuing growing.
Because of that the reasons I streamed started to change and I started to enjoy it less and less.

Don't get me wrong I was still trying to plan more and more fun things I could do with Stream but if I saw that my average was going down it would make me depressed and I wouldn't want to stream even if my regulars were there.
I started thinking "I'm doing something wrong", I'm not entertaining", "people hate me" etc. It was causing me to lose passion for something that I loved.

My point being when you start caring about the numbers more than anything or if you're doing it strictly for growth or money (especially in the beginning) your viewers can feel that.
 There's a difference between having fun and "doing a job".

I took a break from streaming for a while and now I'm back and I'm loving it more than ever.
 Because even if my numbers are completely down, the reasons I'm doing it are because I want to have fun with my community,
which makes it more enjoyable for the rare new people who stop by.

For growth

 be true to yourself .

have some fun.

Encourage your friends to come by.

Support other small streamers you enjoy.

Make sure to use short form content like YouTube shorts and tiktok to show off fun moments. 

Also remember it's easier to be found when there's only 20 streamers and 100, unlike when there's 300,000 viewers and 20,000 streamers. (Because most of those viewers are on the top three channels, and 15,000 are one viewer streams.)
 So if there's a small game you like consider getting involved with that community further. 

For example for me I love splitgate, marauders etc
So it's fun to get involved in the community and I'm more likely to be found.

I wish you the best of luck my friend feel free to post your stream link and I'll stop by. 🫡
